summary: The Rigveda, the oldest layer of Sanskrit literature, takes shape in the northwest of the Indian subcontinent.
title: Vedic hymns compiled (Rigveda)

summary: The early Upanishads articulate atman and brahman — the inner self and ultimate reality — seeding Vedanta and Indian metaphysics.
title: Principal Upanishads composed

summary: Traditionally ascribed to Laozi in the 6th century BCE (modern scholarship favors a 4th–3rd century BCE compilation); the Daodejing founds philosophical Taoism.
title: Tao Te Ching — traditional dating

summary: The Buddha's teaching career establishes the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path; dates follow the traditional long chronology.
title: Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha

summary: Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara, systematizes Jain doctrine: ahimsa and the path to liberation from karma.
title: Mahavira and early Jainism

summary: Confucius teaches ren and li; his sayings, later compiled as the Analects, shape Chinese ethics and statecraft for two millennia.
title: Confucius

summary: Zhuangzi's writings develop Taoist spontaneity and relativism through parables, including the famous butterfly dream.
title: Zhuangzi

summary: The Enochic corpus, including the Book of the Watchers, expands Genesis angelology; it survives whole only in the Ethiopian canon.
title: Book of Enoch (1 Enoch) composed

summary: The rebuilt Temple anchors Jewish worship; the era produces apocalyptic literature and the sectarian movements of the late Second Temple.
title: Second Temple period

summary: Krishna's dialogue with Arjuna on the Kurukshetra field synthesizes the paths of karma, bhakti, and jnana yoga within the Mahabharata.
title: Bhagavad Gita composed

summary: A sectarian community near the Dead Sea copies and stores hundreds of scrolls — biblical, apocryphal, and its own rule books.
title: Qumran community and the Dead Sea Scrolls

summary: Prajnaparamita and other Mahayana sutras appear, introducing emptiness (shunyata) and the bodhisattva ideal.
title: Mahayana sutras emerge

summary: Jesus preaches the Kingdom of God; his crucifixion under Pontius Pilate becomes the founding event of Christianity.
title: Jesus of Nazareth

summary: A sayings gospel of 114 logia attributed to Thomas, preserved in the Nag Hammadi codices; composition estimates range from c. 50 to c. 150 CE.
title: Gospel of Thomas composed

summary: Paul's epistles, the earliest surviving Christian writings, spread the Jesus movement across the Roman Empire.
title: Pauline letters

summary: Greek dialogues attributed to Hermes Trismegistus blend Platonism, Stoicism, and Egyptian religion; they become the core of Western hermeticism.
title: Corpus Hermeticum compiled

summary: The most influential Gnostic teacher develops a sophisticated emanation cosmology; his work survives in fragments quoted by his critics.
title: Valentinus teaches in Rome

summary: Zhang Daoling founds the first organized Taoist church in Sichuan, beginning institutional religious Taoism.
title: Celestial Masters (Tianshi Dao) founded

summary: Patanjali compiles 196 aphorisms systematizing raja yoga — the eight-limbed path from yama to samadhi.
title: Patanjali's Yoga Sutras

summary: Nagarjuna's Mulamadhyamakakarika founds the Middle Way school, the philosophical core of Mahayana Buddhism.
title: Nagarjuna and Madhyamaka

summary: Judah ha-Nasi redacts the Oral Torah into the Mishnah, the foundation of rabbinic Judaism after the Temple's fall.
title: Mishnah compiled

summary: A lengthy Gnostic dialogue in which the risen Jesus instructs his disciples on the soul's ascent through the aeons.
title: Pistis Sophia composed

summary: Thirteen Coptic codices are copied in Upper Egypt, preserving 52 tractates including the Gospels of Thomas and Philip and the Apocryphon of John.
title: Nag Hammadi codices composed

summary: Hermits such as Anthony the Great pioneer Christian monasticism in the Egyptian desert.
title: Desert Fathers

summary: Constantine convenes the first ecumenical council; it produces the Nicene Creed and condemns Arianism.
title: First Council of Nicaea

summary: Augustine's Confessions and City of God shape Western Christian theology of grace, sin, and history.
title: Augustine of Hippo

summary: Yang Xi receives the Shangqing (Highest Clarity) revelations, giving Taoism its great meditation and visualization scriptures.
title: Shangqing revelations

summary: Bishop Athanasius lists the 27 books of the New Testament canon — the first surviving list matching the modern canon.
title: Athanasius' 39th Festal Letter

summary: Likely hidden after Athanasius' canon list delegitimized non-canonical texts, the jarred codices sleep for some 1,500 years.
title: Nag Hammadi codices buried

summary: The second ecumenical council confirms Nicaea and finalizes the Nicene-Constantinopolitan Creed.
title: First Council of Constantinople

summary: The great Buddhist university becomes the intellectual hub of Mahayana and Vajrayana for seven centuries.
title: Nalanda Mahavihara founded

summary: The third and fourth ecumenical councils define Christ's two natures, splitting Eastern and Oriental churches.
title: Councils of Ephesus and Chalcedon

summary: The legendary Indian monk brings dhyana meditation to China, founding the Chan (Zen) lineage.
title: Bodhidharma and Chan

summary: Muhammad receives the Quranic revelations; the text is standardized under the early caliphate.
title: Quran revealed and compiled

summary: Huineng's Platform Sutra proclaims sudden enlightenment, defining Southern Chan and later Zen.
title: Huineng, Sixth Patriarch of Chan

summary: The seventh ecumenical council restores the veneration of icons, closing the Byzantine iconoclast controversy.
title: Second Council of Nicaea

summary: Shankara's commentaries establish non-dual Vedanta — atman is brahman — and he founds four monastic centers.
title: Adi Shankara and Advaita Vedanta

summary: Hermetic texts flourish in Arabic translation; the Emerald Tablet's 'as above, so below' becomes alchemy's motto.
title: Arabic Hermetica and the Emerald Tablet

summary: Atisha's journey to Tibet sparks the second diffusion of Buddhism there and the Kadampa reform movement.
title: Atisha and the later transmission

summary: Ramanuja's qualified non-dualism centers Vedanta on loving devotion (bhakti) to a personal God.
title: Ramanuja and Vishishtadvaita

summary: Al-Ghazali reconciles Sufi mysticism with orthodox theology in the Revival of the Religious Sciences.
title: Al-Ghazali

summary: The 'Greatest Master' expounds wahdat al-wujud, the unity of being, in the Meccan Revelations.
title: Ibn Arabi

summary: Rumi's Masnavi and Divan make divine love the center of Sufi poetry; his followers found the whirling dervishes.
title: Rumi and the Mevlevi order

summary: Moses de León circulates the Zohar, the central text of Kabbalah, ascribed to the 2nd-century Simeon bar Yochai.
title: Zohar circulated

summary: Svatmarama's manual codifies hatha yoga — asana, pranayama, mudras, and the awakening of kundalini.
title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika

summary: Marsilio Ficino's Latin Pimander ignites the Renaissance Hermetic revival under Medici patronage.
title: Ficino translates the Corpus Hermeticum

summary: Pico della Mirandola fuses Hermeticism, Kabbalah, and Platonism, proclaiming humanity's self-fashioning power.
title: Pico's Oration on the Dignity of Man

summary: Blavatsky, Olcott, and Judge found the Society to revive ancient wisdom and investigate the unexplained.
title: Theosophical Society founded

summary: The Secret Doctrine synthesizes science, religion, and philosophy into a cosmic evolutionary scheme of root races.
title: Blavatsky's Secret Doctrine published

summary: The 1893 Parliament introduces Vivekananda's Vedanta and Asian religions to the American public.
title: Parliament of the World's Religions

summary: Farmers find the sealed jar of codices near Jabal al-Tarif, revolutionizing the study of early Christian diversity.
title: Nag Hammadi library discovered

summary: Bedouin shepherds find the first scrolls in Cave 1, opening a window onto Second Temple Judaism.
title: Dead Sea Scrolls discovered
